title: Acid-print HUD: one acid ink on black slabs, giant chamfered numerals with a misregistered plate, the scene as a cold halftone (tactical shooter)
summary: The scene is printed as a cold grey two-ink halftone so it recedes; the HUD uses one acid green on black slabs, red only for damage and danger, giant code-drawn chamfered numerals (the ammo with a second red plate printed out of register), micro labels against them at a poster scale jump, and a kill sticker slapped on at an angle.

provenance.case: tactical-hud round 2 (零点潮汐 NULLTIDE): a 1080p combat HUD, a component state sheet and a 6 s hit-to-kill motion, for an original fictional sci-fi tactical shooter.
provenance.lineage: Bungie's Marathon (2025) graphic-realism UI grammar (one loud ink on black slabs, oversized industrial numerals, tiny technical labels) and Swiss / International-style poster type scale. Borrowed: the grammar. Never borrowed: any Marathon asset, icon, typeface or layout.
provenance.borrow: Borrow grammar, never assets. The scene is the case's own drawn harbour printed through a halftone pass; the numerals are the bank's lettering; every icon is drawn.
provenance.rounds: Round 1 'mil-spec mono' was the safest and could not be told from any HUD kit at 64 px; round 2 took the boldest of six thumbnails. Round 2 first pass: 3 + 5 + 1 findings (still, state sheet, motion) and 4 by eye; final 0.
measured: Round 1 first pass: 14 findings, six of them readouts written straight on the scene with only a text shadow (collage-cover); every readout now has a slab.
Kill notice that faded in was half-transparent over the scene for several frames (3 findings): it now pops in at full opacity.
64 px: the acid numerals and the tilted sticker keep the HUD recognisable; the mono round-1 HUD did not.

acid.use: the one ink: numerals, ready states, the player's kill row, the sticker

red.use: damage, enemies, low ammo or HP, the misregistered plate

scene.use: the scene placeholder's ground tone (a cold grey halftone)

sans.use: names, labels and the kill word (900), micro labels (600, tracked .08em)

num.use: small numbers, codes, Latin labels; never CJK (a Barlow 爆头 lost its glyphs in round 1)

fonts.resolve: fonts query --text-file <all HUD copy> --style gothic --weight 700 resolves Noto Sans SC (the case's query); Barlow Condensed is Latin only (fonts measure --path).
fonts.licence: All roles use SIL OFL 1.1 fonts.
fonts.lettering: HP, ammo and scores are the bank's lettering: width 0.55, stroke 0.19, chamfer 0.12 diagonal, slant 0.1, sidebearing 0.05, tracking 20.
fonts.note: Fonts are named, not bundled. --font-dir <dir> reads coverage and embeds the faces.

grammar: One dominant ink (acid) on black slabs; red only for damage, enemies and low states.
Two giant code-drawn numerals (HP, ammo) against 15 px micro labels: a scale jump of 1:7 to 1:11.
The ammo numeral is printed over a second red plate 6-7 px off; the plates swap when ammo is low.
Nothing small sits on the scene: every readout has its own 88% black slab.
One broken-grid move: the vitals slab tilts from its bottom-left corner; the kill notice is a sticker slapped on at an angle with a red offset plate.
The scene is printed as a cold two-ink halftone so the HUD is always the loudest thing.

procedural: chamfered numerals with a misregistered plate (Doc.lettering shadow plate)
icon family on a 48 grid, each with one 45-degree 'tide cut' notch: smoke, dash, pulse, overdrive, grenade, rifle and pistol silhouettes
minimap blocks, compass ticks, magazine ticks, barcode, shield cells (skewed -24 degrees)
recipes: Scene as a cold halftone: materials process --file <scene.png> --effect halftone --params '{"periodPx":8,"angleDeg":45,"ink":"#2E302C","paper":"none","contrast":1.1}' --seed 1 over a #8E918A ground (the case used its own two-ink AM screen: 45 degrees, 8 px grid, paper noise), then the scene slot.
A second plate for print texture: materials process --effect duotone --params '{"inks":["#2E302C","#5A5E57"],"angles":[45,15],"periodPx":8}'.
collage: The scene is the only image and nothing small is written on it.
materials.sources: Everything is drawn; the scene is your game's frame.

grammar: Hit to kill in 6 s: two hits, shield shatters, the HP lag segment drains 0.4 s after the hit, return fire, kill, double kill, shield regenerates.
The kill sticker pops in scaled 1.15 to 1 at full opacity: never fade text in over the scene.
Damage arcs and the red edge fade over 0.6 s; numerals change by hard cuts, no rolling counters.
motion.flashLimit: Red edge flashes stay under three per second.

guidance: 64 px distinctiveness (guidance): shrink to 64 px beside a generic HUD kit; the acid numerals and the tilted sticker should still read. A mono, evenly-weighted HUD does not.
Check the HUD on real 3D frames before shipping: the case only verified it over a drawn, halftoned harbour.
At 50% (a 960x540 capture) micro labels drop under 12 px: give a separate small-screen layout rather than scaling (the case's 50% readability table).
checks.note: The browser check runs on every render (slabs, sticker and misregistered plate are measured in pixels).

examples.note: Renders of the case that stay examples: see docs/cases/tactical-hud/ (README showcase).

renders.screen: component state sheet (shield broken, critical HP, low ammo, reload, abilities)
renders.why: a review sheet, not a screen; the states are parameters of hud.combat (ability states, HP and ammo thresholds)
